newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends sharply up on Canada shipping woes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends sharply up on Canada shipping woes.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed sharply higher on prospects for a shift in wheat business away from Canada to the U.S., traders said.
Shipping problems in Canada prompted the Board of Directors of Saskatchewan Wheat Pool Tuesday to request an emergency meeting to address grain transportation difficulties on the prairies.

There was news early Tuesday the Canadian Wheat Board passed on February-March delivery period sales, but Lorne Hehn, CWB chief commissioner, told Reuters no Asian vessels berthed in Vancouver have been diverted to the U.S.
The commissioner also said Canadian spring wheat exports in April may be hurt by a rail shipping delay that has kept more than 1.5 million tonnes of grain from reaching Pacific ports since January.
Aggressive fund buying in late dealings kicked wheat into fast trading in the nearby three months but the demand was centered in the March, the key old crop CBOT wheat contract.
Rosenthal Collins and Prudential Securities each bought at least five million bushels of March in late trading.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 9-1/2 at $3.62.
March wheat set a new contract low early on persistent reminders of the large supply of wheat worldwide amid only routine export business, traders said.
The new low for March is $3.51 per bushel, below the previous low of $3.52 posted Monday.

Traders and analysts have said USDA in its February supply/demand report slated for release at 0730 CST Wednesday may increase its estimate for the Australian wheat crop. There were some ideas USDA may hike by one million tonnes its outlook for Australia's crop.
USDA in January pegged Australia's crop at 21.5 million tonnes. The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) pegged the crop at 23.226 million tonnes.

Chartists pointed to the technically oversold condition of the wheat market with the nine day relative strength index (RSI) of the March at 27 percent at midsession. But by the close the March RSI surged to nearly neutral territory at 45 percent. The market generally considers a market as oversold at an RSI of 30 or less.
Early Tuesday first support in the March was at $3.49-1/2 and second support was at $3.42. The session low for March was $3.51, its contract low. The session high was $3.63.
First resistance was at $3.58 and second resistance was at $3.66-1/2.
Key four and 20-day moving averages continued to emit bearish signals, technicians reported.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,500 contracts, above the 14,998 traded Monday.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, above the 2,668 traded Monday.
